eras._note:
Era 1 (1999-2001), the frameset site, one page per stage and per sector. Each is a five-column table -- logo, YEAR FUNDED, company, product, STATUS ('IPO 1984', 'Acquired by Maxwell-Macmillan 1987') -- and the company cell is identified by the YEAR CELL BEFORE IT, not by its own markup: the year, product and status cells share its shape exactly, and an earlier pattern keyed on the

that only some name cells carry returned 6 rows of 90. This is the 1965-2000 book (Mentor Graphics 1981, Banyan 1983, Continental Cablevision). The /company/recent_page1.htm page of the same era is prose, not a table, and its rows reappear on era 2. The year and status columns are parsed separately into sources/site/archive-cards.json by scratch/build-archive-cards.py.

Era 1's PUBLIC page is the firm's own IPO roster and it needs its own pattern: the row is company | TICKER | IPO DATE | IPO SIZE, so there is no four-digit year cell for the era pattern to anchor on and the page parsed to zero. Anchoring on the ticker-then-date pair recovers 155 rows with the firm's own IPO dates and sizes — the survivorship surface for everything that reached the public market before 2001.

Era 1's MERGERS page inverts the column order of every other page in its era, and that inversion is an acquirer-mark trap. The stage and sector pages run logo | YEAR | company | product | status, so the era pattern takes the cell AFTER the year; this page runs logo | company | YEAR | ACQUIRER, so the same pattern harvested 45 acquirers as portfolio rows -- ADP, Cisco, IBM, Lotus, Lucent, Pfizer, Siemens, Sun Microsystems, Westinghouse. That is COLLECTION.md §5's First Round acquirer-mark class arriving through a column order rather than a logo wall. This pattern takes the cell BEFORE the year instead.

Era 2 (2001-2003), the ASP site. Five alphabetical slices of one book, each row a logo+name anchor with class=companylink plus FOCUS, STATUS (Private/Public/Acquired) and the YEAR of the investment. The negative lookahead drops the A-D/E-H pagination links, which carry the same class. The logo filename is NOT taken as the slug (COLLECTION.md sec 5, the Lux rule that the row's own text wins): the firm's files carry a size suffix ('athoc_65.gif'), so an alt-first read publishes '@Hoc' as 'athoc_65'.
Era 2's 'Other Investments' page: the positions outside the six sector buckets, on no ByName slice.

Era 3 (2005-2010), the ColdFusion site. cat=AllInvest renders the whole book on one page; the bare portfolio.cfm is only the category menu. Each row is a <div class="data"> carrying the name in <div class="dataHead">, the website, a description, 'Status:', 'Year Funded:', the GREYLOCK PARTNER on the deal (a link to team/bio.cfm) and a Region.

Era 4 (2011-2014), the Rails site. The sector parameter filters client-side, so any sector page ships the WHOLE book (230 rows in 2011) as <a href="/companies/<id>" class="show_company">; rows with a logo carry no anchor text and the name comes from the img alt ('Web-1000-memories'), rows without one carry the plain name. The numeric ids make cdx_company_pages useless for this era. Widened to 2014 after Common Crawl showed the sector pages still server-rendering the whole book in 2013 and 2014 (268 show_company anchors on a 2014-09 capture); the Internet Archive enumerated those two years thinly.

Era 5 (2018-2025), the WordPress site's single /portfolio/ page. Only the FEATURED companies get a logo-wall anchor carrying both identities (href="#<slug>-div" plus a visually-hidden name); the rest of the page's 427 visually-hidden spans are social URLs, so this era contributes about a dozen rows and the era's real enumeration is era 6's CDX sweep of /portfolio/<slug> plus Common Crawl.

Era 5b (2018-2023), the same WordPress /portfolio page read through the firm's own UPLOAD FILENAMES. Its rows render as logo images with an EMPTY alt, so the visually-hidden-span pattern of era 5 sees only the dozen featured companies while the wall itself carries 86 more -- and the file names are the firm's own ('Abnormal-Security-Listing-181x115.png', 'Grand-Rounds-Listing-181x115.png'), which is the COLLECTION.md logo-era rule. The '-Listing' infix is what separates portfolio logos from every other image the theme ships. Note the path has NO trailing slash so it does not collide with era 5's own snapshot memo; both eras read the same page and their rows merge per year on slug+path. Rows recovered here that no later surface carries: Bounty Jobs, Caavo, Convoy, Creative Live, Crew, Grand Rounds, Latent Space.

Era 6 (2017-2026), the per-company pages of the WordPress site and of the Next.js/Sanity site that replaced it in 2026. Same /portfolio/<slug> namespace across both, so one CDX enumeration covers the handover.

roster._note: Four people namespaces over the site's life: /team/*.htm and /team/default.asp (1998-2004), /team/bio.cfm?Id=<n> (2005-2010, numeric and not slug-enumerable), /teams/<slug> (2011-2014) and /team/<slug> (2015-2026). The live roster is the Sanity teamMember type, which carries category ('Investors') and a departed flag, so current and alumni separate without a tenure guess. The Sanity `category` field is the site's own grouping -- Investors (19), EIRs (12), Emeritus (9), Venture Partners (6), Advisory Partners (3), Specialists (5), Operations (5) -- and site_team_groups keeps the four investing ones. EIRs are excluded on the a16z rule: an executive in residence is a related person on their own next company's Form D, which is a founder seat, not a firm position. The Sanity alias is `group`, not `site_group`: partner-roster.py reads r['group'] when it applies site_team_groups, and a differently named key silently disables the filter -- which on this firm would sweep the EIR directory (Nir Zuk of Palo Alto Networks, Jeff Weiner of LinkedIn, Glenn Kelman of Redfin, David McJannet of HashiCorp), the First Round founder-directory trap arriving through a group label instead of a case rule. Five ungrouped names (Cyrus Pinto, Dwane Hamilton, John Delaney, Julie Smith, Katy Amaya) carry no Sanity category at all, so site_team_groups cannot see them and they reached the Form D sweep: John Delaney confirmed Alliance Partners LLC and Julie Smith confirmed Carbon Health and e-Scape Bio, each on a common-name match against a company neither Greylock nor that person has any position in. They and the EIR directory are excluded BY NAME in not_a_person, which is the First Round remedy applied through the only lever the roster config offers when the group label is missing.

site_api._note: greylock.com is Next.js on Vercel over a PUBLIC Sanity dataset (project uz672vkd, dataset production), so the ladder stops at step 2. portfolioCompany carries the firm's own ENTRY ROUND (firstPartnered), a status, the headquarters string, the deal partners as references and a category; teamMember carries the roster with a departed flag. The live surface is only 158 rows for a firm founded in 1965 -- the archive eras are where the book is, and the site also serves a markdown alternate (/portfolio.md) that renders the same table. A second source, archive-cards.json, is the SAME first-party listings read for their other columns: scratch/build-archive-cards.py parses the firm's own YEAR FUNDED, status line, deal partner and region out of the 1999-2001, 2001-2003, 2005-2010 and 2011-2014 captures (456 companies, investment years 1967-2007). wayback-pull's listing_regex keeps slug and name only, so without this the firm's own dated record of its pre-window book would be discarded by the layer best placed to supply it. Membership is unchanged -- these rows ARE listings on the investor's own site under COLLECTION.md §1's evidence sufficiency, any era -- and the status wording is evidence for the judge, never a label.

edgar._note: 'Greylock' alone is unusable as an EDGAR full-text phrase: Greylock Capital Management (New York, Hans Humes) runs an unrelated distressed-debt and emerging-markets fund family under the same word, so the phrases are entity-qualified to the venture partnerships. Namesakes on EDGAR: the Greylock Global / Emerging Markets / Distressed Debt funds (NY and Cayman), Greylock Marketing Inc and Greylock Inc (Florida), Greylock Ventures LP - IAI-1 Series (Maryland).

desks._note: One home desk. The venture partnerships file from Boston (One Federal Street, then 880 Winter Street, Waltham) and later California (2550 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park). Desks resolve by CIK and filing address, never by the word alone -- three namesakes share it and one of them nearly took a home fund with it: GREYLOCK CAPITAL LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (CIK 940543) files from One Federal Street, Boston and is a Greylock Partners vehicle, while Greylock Capital MANAGEMENT (New York, Hans Humes) runs the unrelated Greylock Global / Emerging Markets / Distressed Debt family; a 'greylock capital' external pattern classed the Boston fund out on the first pass. The other namesakes: Greylock Investments SLP (Aztec Group House, St Helier, Jersey; related persons Richard Phillips and Liam Jones, no Greylock Partners connection), Greylock Marketing Inc and Greylock Inc (Florida). GREYLOCK ISRAEL L P (CIK 1370903, Ugland House, Grand Cayman) and the 83North entities are the T1 boundary question and are ruled in decisions.md, not by this pattern list. GREYLOCK VENTURES LIMITED PARTNERSHIP - IAI-1 SERIES (CIK 1921288) went the other way on the second pass and is HOME: its related person Donald Sullivan is Greylock's own operations partner -- the firm's 2011-2014 site names him as the Greylock partner on Lytro -- and its GP, 'Greylock Ventures GP LLC - Series IAI-1', follows the firm's own GP naming. The Burlington MA address is a fund administrator's, not a namesake's. It is a series SPV, filed 2022, Indefinite offering, $0 sold.

profile._note: focus_min_companies 25, about 4.5% of the 561-row base. The crosswalk maps the firm's own seven portfolioCategory values; 'Other' maps to nothing. The recompute reports no values above the threshold because those tags cover only the 158 LIVE rows -- 28% of the base -- and the sector signal for the other 403 comes from the grind's focus column, not from a site tag. The curated list is therefore kept and reconciled against the landed distribution by hand, which is what the sidecar's reconciliation flag records.

socials_gap.note: 32 of 52 published people carry a link after the site read, the outside pages and the checked search (26 searched, 6 found); recorded by site-portfolio.py --record-gap

shape._note: c2a_rate_max raised from the 0.80 default to 0.98 for this investor, restated against the evidence rather than waived (§8, the Thrive rule). Greylock's base carries 79 Seed entries and only 34 of them are in the C2A cohort: the rest are censored, under 24 months from entry with no resolution. What survives that filter is the establishable set, and on a firm whose seed book is dominated by 2020-2025 AI companies that all raised an A within a year, the establishable set is almost entirely graduations — 33 of 34. The published rate carries that bias in its own sentence (§6): 'of the seed entries where the record could be established, ~97% graduated; the establishable set skews toward visible successes, and half the seed book is too young to be in it at all.' one_b_share_max is left at the 0.20 default and the base passes it. Re-derived 2026-09-17 under the status contract (D-S2A in decisions.md), since the reasoning above counted a cohort of unverified rows: the re-judged book is 71 seed entries, 10 censored, 22 undetermined, cohort 39 at 94.9% with 64% coverage. The shape the old note described survives the harder instrument -- a seed book dominated by 2020-2025 AI companies that raised an A within a year, where what can be established is almost entirely graduations -- so the 0.98 ceiling stands unchanged and the published sentence now carries the coverage as well as the bias. S2A ceiling restated 2026-09-21 under PRO-132, where every Seed row is decided (coverage 100% by construction): 61 seed entries, 10 censored, cohort 51 at 84.3% (43 graduated, 8 not). The 0.98 ceiling was set against a cohort that held only the establishable seeds; with the non-graduations counted the rate sits just above the 0.80 default, so the guard is restated to 0.90 rather than left where it cannot fire.
